decisions.summary: No make target formats one file; filed as T34, landing before T22.
decisions.why: A tooling gap rather than a defect; filing it narrows nothing of the request.

decisions.summary: A found-and-left item that says it is fixed in the task (fixed here, fixed in this task, before its tick, before T<own> lands) passes without a reason, filed id and order, unless it names an id it is filed as or lands before.
decisions.why: D15's visible sentence requires every non-none item to carry reason, id and order, so this narrows D15's text. But FR-009 refuses only an item that DEFERS a defect, and an item fixed in the task defers nothing; the GM approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task', so requiring a filed task id of an item that is fixed would contradict the request. The guard that an item naming a filed/order id is judged as a deferral keeps the pass from being used to hide one.

decisions.summary: An item that says it is not a defect (not a defect, no wrong outcome, constitution XIV) passes.
decisions.why: Narrows D15's 'any non-none item' wording, but FR-009's own words reach only an item that 'defers a defect', and constitution XIV (the GM 2026-11-19) holds that a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect and is not to be fixed. Demanding a filed fix task for a non-defect would apply a standard the GM struck. Same id-naming guard applies.

decisions.summary: A deferral owes 'Not fixed here' plus two words of reason, filed as T<n> (or added to / folded into), lands before T<m> (lists read whole), order id not equal to filed id, each id a box of tasks.md or tasks-done.md; make decide adds that each id is an unticked box now.
decisions.why: This is FR-009's three parts (why, filed id, order) made checkable; added to / folded into still name a filed task id; the open test at make decide makes the order real enforcement as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A class fix is detected by every/all the before writer, reader, form, file, caller, instance, copy, site or guard, or 'each of the', and then owes an observed/measured line with its method.
decisions.why: FR-009's named forms (every writer, every form, every file of a kind) are all reached and the list is a superset of them; a mechanical trigger has to be a word test, and nothing FR-009 names falls outside it.

decisions.summary: The class test reads the found-and-left items and checklist item 12 (Before any fix).
decisions.why: FR-009 asks about the section's FIX; in the plan template the fix is declared in item 12 and the found-and-left answer, so reading those is reading the fix.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta runs the timeless half (form and ids filed in tasks.md or tasks-done.md) on a changed block; a section whose deferral's task has since landed is not refused.
decisions.why: FR-009 names make decide; running the same rule on a later edit only enforces it against a decided section being changed into an unformed one (the GM: 'real enforcement and not just instructions'). Not requiring the ids to be open after landing narrows nothing FR-009 asks, which is a check at decision time.

decisions.summary: A section decided under DEFER_FORM_OK passes make plan-delta after its block changes, the escape found in the guard log; the escape excuses only deferral findings.
decisions.why: It relaxes only the plan-delta check, which is enforcement beyond FR-009's make decide; at make decide, where FR-009 places the refusal, nothing is relaxed, and the escape was recorded with its reason as FR-012 requires.

decisions.summary: The tool records DEFER_FORM_OK itself (guard log rule defer-form-ok and dev/bypass-log/) instead of D15's $(LOGESCAPE) line, and only on a run that passes (decide once decided, plan-delta only where it excused a finding); a thin reason is refused.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of two words or more that is recorded; it is recorded, once, whenever it is used. A run that is refused or excuses nothing did not use the escape. Mechanism choice; D15's text is restated to match (found-and-left).

decisions.summary: make plan-delta reads the guard log only for a changed block with a deferral finding, once a run, parsing only files naming the rule.
decisions.why: A cost choice that changes no outcome.

decisions.summary: plan-done.md is never read by make decide or plan-delta and the tick and landing call neither, so the 28 refused archived sections are not re-judged.
decisions.why: FR-009 is a refusal at make decide of a section being decided; archived sections were decided and ticked before the rule existed and no make decide runs on them. Nothing FR-009 asks is left out.

decisions.summary: Makefile FREE_TEXT and help lines for DEFER_FORM_OK, D15 restated, docs/guards.md row and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md plan row are fixed by the session before T17 lands, outside the builder's brief.
decisions.why: Fixed before the task lands, not deferred; matches the GM-approved default of fixing in the task.

decisions.summary: T17 is tagged [perf] under FR-013.
decisions.why: It is improvement 4 of the six the GM ordered first on 2026-11-20 ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), and it shortens the builders' loop, which FR-013 names.

decisions.summary: a new guard context_cap_hooks, PreToolUse *, after event_log_hooks in guards(); its files held by make guard-edit
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for a guard refusing a builder's tool call past a threshold; this is where and how it is placed. Nothing the request or FR-006 says is narrowed.

decisions.summary: payloads captured from Claude Code itself (claude -p, a scratch hook) rather than a dump in the clone, pinned as payloads.json
decisions.why: A method for finding the payload's real keys (agent_id, agent_type, transcript_path), labeled with date and method; it decides nothing about what is refused.

decisions.summary: no agent_id passes before any read (main session); an agent_type naming the clone's .claude/agents/<type>.md passes on a stat
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as an agent with a task's brief, not a defined review agent; the main session is not an agent. Carries D8 as accepted.

decisions.summary: an agent_id that is not letters, digits, - and _ passes
decisions.why: Both the cap's measure (the transcript at subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl) and its one exit (the handoff file named by the agent id) are paths built from the id; an id that cannot be joined into a path leaves neither a context to measure nor a handoff to name, so refusing would refuse with no exit. The same capture shows builders' ids are plain names, so ordinary work does not reach this path and FR-006's enforcement is not gutted.

decisions.summary: context = input + cache_read + cache_creation tokens of the last assistant row with usage above zero; user rows carrying a child's usage and zero rows skipped
decisions.why: FR-006 caps the builder's context; this measures the builder's own model call and excludes rows that are not its model calls (measured: user rows hold the child's usage). It makes the cap measure what FR-006 names.

decisions.summary: no transcript file, or no such row in the tail, passes
decisions.why: Where no context is recorded there is no figure to compare with FR-006's threshold; refusing on no evidence would refuse builders that are under it. The capture (2026-11-20) shows the transcript exists beside transcript_path for a builder, so ordinary work does not reach this path and the request's 'real enforcement' holds.

decisions.summary: the tail is read backwards in 64 KiB steps to at most 16 MiB (both GUESS; the 16 MiB now labeled with the window's largest builder transcript, 50 MB scanned whole in 0.07 s, measured 2026-11-20, research R2); a builder whose last usage row lies further back passes
decisions.why: What lies after the last assistant row is that turn's tool results; 16 MiB of them with no assistant row between is not a shape ordinary work produces, so a builder past the cap is not let through by it in practice. The bound is a labeled GUESS knob, and the figure now beside it (a whole 50 MB transcript scanned in 0.07 s) is labeled with date and method; it speaks to cost, not to how far back a last usage row can sit, so it neither strengthens nor weakens this ruling. Not measured that no real tail exceeds 16 MiB - worth a count from the event log when the knob is retuned, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS GUESS 300,000; at the cap passes
decisions.why: FR-006's own knob and value, labeled GUESS.

decisions.summary: past the cap every call is refused but the handoff file's Write, the refusal naming the file and the next step (write what is done and left, stop, reply with the path; the session dispatches a fresh builder)
decisions.why: FR-006 verbatim ('but for writing its handoff file, naming the file and the next step'), and the approved improvement 1 ('a fresh builder per stage, with a handoff file').

decisions.summary: an Edit of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Implied by FR-006's own words: the exception is 'writing its handoff file', and an Edit of that file is writing it. Confined to the agent's own handoff, it cannot carry task work, so the cap's purpose (no builder works on past a large context) survives.

decisions.summary: a Read of the handoff file is let through beside its Write
decisions.why: Ground that holds regardless of the stated tool behavior: a Read confined to the agent's own handoff file yields only what the builder itself wrote there, so it cannot carry task work and does not gut the cap's purpose, while the stated reason (the Write tool will not overwrite an unread file) would otherwise leave a builder with an existing handoff no exit. That premise about the Write tool carries no date and method in the block; it is not what this ruling rests on.

decisions.summary: any file in <git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/ whose name ends <agent id>.md counts as the agent's handoff
decisions.why: Applying the literal one-name rule, recomputed at each call from the event log's task, could refuse the very file the refusal named if the chain's task moved between them, leaving the builder no exit - defeating FR-006's handoff. Agent ids are unique, so no builder can write another's handoff (a case the suite refuses), and every such file sits in the handoff directory, where writing cannot carry task work. Ruled as stated, 'any file there' = in that directory. On the earlier aside: the session reports is_handoff compares the canonicalized parent directory with the handoff directory, so a path such as l7r-handoffs/../x-<id>.md resolves outside it and is refused; the carve-out stays confined to that directory.

decisions.summary: the handoff is named <task>-<agent id>.md from the event log's chain (filed_at), or <agent id>.md where the line carries no task
decisions.why: Naming the file FR-006 requires; no case is excused.

decisions.summary: a call outside any clone passes
decisions.why: On what the block establishes: D8's test of who is a builder is a stat of the clone's .claude/agents/, and the handoff path is under the clone's git common dir; outside a clone there is neither a who nor an exit to name, so a refusal there could refuse defined review agents and leave a builder no handoff to write. The premise that builders' calls are made inside clones in ordinary work is not measured in the block and no suite case is listed for this path - worth a count, not a block.

decisions.summary: CONTEXT_OK="<reason>" in a Bash command, recorded as context-ok; a bare one refused
decisions.why: FR-012: an escape of a reason of two words or more, recorded.

decisions.summary: D9's make context-ok AID= WHY= per-agent permit not built in T12; filed as T13, to land before T22; CONTEXT_OK in Bash the recorded escape meanwhile
decisions.why: Judged against FR-012, not D9 (which this task restated): every refusal the cap issues today has a recorded route past it - the refusal's compliant step (the handoff, always let through) and CONTEXT_OK in a Bash call, recorded - so FR-012's escape exists and no builder is trapped. The permit was the session's design for a resumed builder (D10's resume); it is filed and ordered, not dropped. Nothing the GM asked for is left out.

decisions.summary: in the performance lane after T15 and T16, before T13
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM 2026-11-20 ('let's prioritize those remaining improvement fixes'); T12 is improvement 1.

decisions.summary: red-first unit and suite runs, the check-deleted run red, and the handoff Write's case through the whole guard chain
decisions.why: FR-012's red-first test and D9's whole-chain case; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: docs/guards.md row and knob-table row, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md mention, D9 restated to what was built, written by the session before the tick
decisions.why: D14's knob table and keeping the spec true to the built guard; no behavior added or excused.

decisions.summary: D10 in context_cap_hooks: a SendMessage resuming a builder past the cap, or whose task has landed since its dispatch, is refused; escape CONTEXT_OK in the summary, recorded
decisions.why: FR-006 and D10 verbatim; FR-012's red-first, recorded escape; serves the approved improvement 1 ('a fresh builder per stage').

decisions.summary: The sender's own cap is judged before resume(): a builder past its cap is refused its SendMessage like any call
decisions.why: D9 already refuses every tool call of a builder past the cap but the handoff write; this only orders the two checks.

decisions.summary: A SendMessage to an id with no agent-<to>.meta.json passes, logged resume-no-meta

decisions.summary: No task found by D2's chain: under the cap passes with a no-task record; past the cap refused
decisions.why: The landed test needs a task and cannot apply without one; the cap clause of FR-006 still applies and is kept (the cap check needs no task). The pass is recorded.

decisions.summary: The target's task: the brief's T<n>, else its first line's task (by/aid), else the task-starts entry in force at its dispatch - never the latest start
decisions.why: D2's chain read for the builder's own task; using the start in force at dispatch rather than the latest start serves FR-006's 'its task' and avoids attributing another, later task to it.

decisions.summary: Landed = an end line with landed true naming the task after the dispatch (a background land included; a refused landing does not count), or the task ticked in tasks.md/tasks-done.md
decisions.why: FR-006 says 'whose task has landed' with no time bound; D10 adds 'since it was dispatched'. A ticked task is a landed one (make land ticks). Counting a ticked task without the dispatch bound stays inside FR-006's wording and does not narrow what is refused.

decisions.summary: Dispatch time: the Agent line whose id is the meta's toolUseId, else the builder's first line, else its transcript's first timestamp

decisions.why: Dependencies on the line's task and the land end line; FR-013 counts work making the builders' loop faster as performance work.

decisions.summary: Run every line `make -n quick` lists (all seven checks) after the filing, setting aside only the green stamp and the closing printf; no skip list of checks deemed unable to read what task-add writes.
decisions.why: The request (improvement 6) says 'run make quick after task-add' and FR-011 says task-add runs make quick's checks. Every check runs. The stamp and the printf are not checks: the stamp records a green state for the tree, and the printf prints a message. Leaving both out catches nothing less. Dropping the skip list widens what is checked rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: The kept lines run side by side, each by sh -c to its own end, read from the make -n listing (backslash continuations joined) so the recipe stays the one list.
decisions.why: This is how the checks are run, not which checks run. Running each line to its own end shows every failure, including one that a sequential make quick would hide behind an earlier red. That serves FR-011's 'on any failure the new line introduces'.

decisions.summary: On a red, both files are restored to their pre-filing bytes, the checks are re-run, and failures (failed (exit N) plus each non-blank line, with only line/column numbers masked) are compared as multisets. A failure only in the with-line run keeps the line withdrawn and refuses (exit 2), naming it. Otherwise the line is restored and the red is reported as already there.
decisions.why: This is FR-011 (withdraw and refuse, naming the failure, on a failure the new line introduces). The masking cannot hide a new failure: an identical message at a shifted line is still counted twice in the multiset, and only line/column digits are masked, so ids such as FR-023 and FR-024 stay distinct. The pre-existing case keeps the line, as FR-011 limits refusal to failures the new line introduces.

decisions.summary: A make -n quick that cannot list (no Makefile) refuses before anything is written.
decisions.why: Fails closed. Without a listing the requested check cannot run, so filing anyway would skip the enforcement the GM asked to be real. It adds no reach beyond FR-011.

decisions.summary: The QUICK_OK escape is read from the environment and recorded by the task-add tool itself (escaped/quick-ok in the guard log), not through the Makefile's $(LOGESCAPE), following T28's PERF_LATER_OK precedent. The Makefile's FREE_TEXT entry and help line are done by the lead.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for an escape of a reason that is recorded. It is recorded, once, and a real-tree probe confirmed the row (escaped/quick-ok). The choice changes where the recording happens, not what is enforced or what can be escaped, so it does not narrow the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: The escape reason must be two words and eight characters, else refused blocked/QUICK_OK-no-reason before anything is written.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for 'a reason of two words or more'. Requiring eight characters as well makes the escape harder to use, which does not narrow the enforcement. The GM asked that enforcement be real (2026-11-19 approval).

decisions.summary: Tests: the four red-first cases, the check-deleted run (five red), the every-line pin (the ruff line asserted run), and the guard-log isolation pin.
decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-011 and FR-012's red-first requirement. Each test only fails when the requested behavior is absent.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the two real-tree probe rows in ~/.claude/guard-log and the rust/gate/CLAUDE.md task row not naming task_add/quick.rs are judged not defects.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome. The log rows are the measurement's own records, in an untracked log. The index line misdirects no tool and blocks no work. The QUICK_OK help/FREE_TEXT gap is fixed in this task, not deferred.

decisions.summary: T20 builds the shard form only, proved on test-parts.sh (split 6 + 7 cases plus 16 new pins); the three slow suites' splits, entry-gate.sh included, are T21's, landing before T22
decisions.why: D17 settles exactly this split of work: 'T20 builds the form, proved on test-parts.sh; T21 splits the three'. The found-and-left entry-gate deferral is that same assignment, not a defect left; every case of test-parts.sh still runs (13 before, 6 + 23 after).

decisions.summary: A shard is tests/hooks/test-<name>.<k>.sh with k all digits, run in numeric order with gaps allowed; each shard is its own job <guard>.<k> with its own .rc/.log/.s/.reads and stamps nothing
decisions.why: D17's 'tests/hooks/test-<name>.<k>.sh ... treats each shard as a job keyed by the suite's stamp key'; the per-shard .s is the measure D17 and SC-004 name.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh --close stamps the suite (sha, trace from every shard's reads, shard list .jobs) only when every shard's job is ok; one red or missing shard leaves it unstamped
decisions.why: D17: 'stamps the suite green when every shard is'. One stamp per suite is the mechanism that delivers that without losing shards' reads.

decisions.summary: Recipe keys each shard as its own name via deps --keys and hashes the guard's key with its shards' keys; an edited or added shard reruns the suite; no change to rust/guard
decisions.why: Implementation of D17's 'keyed by the suite's stamp key'; it keeps the skip-when-unchanged behavior correct for shards and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: GUARD WITHOUT A TEST accepts a guard's suite or its shards (one hookrun.sh --jobs call); a suite beside its own shards fails as SUITE AND SHARDS BOTH; an orphan shard fails as SHARD WITHOUT ITS SUITE; a single-shard guard is accepted
decisions.why: D17: 'its companion check accepts shards for a guard's companion' and shards sit 'beside nothing else of that name'. The two refusals only fail when D17's form is broken, so they enforce what was asked.

decisions.summary: test-land-tooling.sh case 2b's wall-clock overlap bound (.checks < 1.8) is replaced by a barrier: each job marks its start and waits up to 20 s for the other's mark, and the case asserts both saw the other; timings stay recorded as numbers
decisions.why: A check that refused correct work under load (3 of 3 failed at load, recorded) is a defect, and fixing it is owed under fix-as-we-go. It still enforces the same property, that the two jobs overlap: run one after the other it went red 2 of 2. It narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: T20 expects no wall saving (parts.sh was never on the critical path); the saving is T21's; before/after equal within noise
decisions.why: It follows from D17's T20/T21 division; FR-010's 20 s bar is met by T21's splits, and SHARD_BAR_S is never a gate per D17.

decisions.summary: One environment reader for the guard crate, shared::env (opt, var; test-build set, unset): the process variable outside cfg(test), a per-test-thread map under it; consulted::var and VARS become re-exports of it (T24's seam, one map); arbiter/tests.rs pins the seam.
decisions.why: Implementation design of the fix T32 exists for. The defect is a wrong outcome: guard tests go red because a page session's shell exports a variable. A builder no longer losing rounds to that red serves the GM's 2026-11-20 request to put performance improvements first (FR-013: the builders' loop). Nothing the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Fix the 6 tests that the 79-variable sweep showed moving (RECORD_CHECKS_DIR, L7R_GUARD_TREE, SET_DOWN_ROOT, L7R_PERMIT_NOW x2, L7R_DISPATCHER), and stop the event-log tests writing fixture logs into an exported L7R_EVENTS_DIR.
decisions.why: Known defects of the same kind, fixed in the task that found them (fix as we go). The stray event-log writes matter directly to this feature, because they corrupt the logs that where-time and the GM's retrospective read.

decisions.summary: Convert the 7 tests that set the process environment to set the test thread's own map, converting their reads with them.
decisions.why: Same mechanism, same task. It widens no behavior beyond the guard crate's tests.

decisions.summary: Leave log::quiet's GUARD_LOG_DIR set once for the whole process (T009), and leave the binary's main.rs and bench.rs reading the real environment.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome. GUARD_LOG_DIR is set once on purpose, to keep test logs out of real ones. main.rs and bench.rs are not tests and must read the real environment. The GM's request asks for no rule against process-environment mutation; that wording is the task line's own. Leaving a difference that works is not a narrowing (constitution XIV).

decisions.summary: Leave MEASURE_STATE_DIR (a test created the directory empty and wrote nothing into it) and the reads that the sweep showed moving no test, as not defects.
decisions.why: Measured to produce no wrong outcome (ls of the exported directory; per-var.tsv). Under constitution XIV these are not defects, and nothing the GM asked is left undone.

decisions.summary: The gate crates' tests reading the real environment through the guard (49 tests in 7 crates red with L7R_FEATURE_DIRECTORY and L7R_EVENTS_DIR exported) are not fixed in T32. They are filed as T38, ordered to land before T22, with the reason stated: the guard's test map is cfg(test) of the guard alone, so the fix is a reader threaded to 17 call sites in 7 crates, each owing its own test, lint and cover.
decisions.why: The defect is not dropped or left unfixed in the feature. It is scheduled as its own task in the same feature, with a stated reason and an ordering, which is what FR-009 requires of a deferral. T32's filed scope is the guard crate's own tests, so moving work outside that crate into a separate task narrows nothing the GM asked for. This would be a finding only if T38 were not performance-tagged or never landed, and this block cannot show either.

decisions.summary: no_poll_hooks, named by T14's run, is not fixed: it failed in none of 4 exported runs and none of the sweep's 91, and it is named in the report.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome was reproduced, so no known defect is left. Naming it in the report is the honest handling.

decisions.summary: T32 is classed as performance work ([perf], FR-013): a builder's make rust-test on the guard is green whatever the session exports.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts 'the builders' loop faster' as performance work. A false red that costs a builder a round falls inside that definition and inside the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'.

decisions.summary: Order: after T24 (its seam is reused), independent of T20. Exits: crate-scoped lint and cover, make quick, make static once, make hooks-test; on red, the task is set down and any claim that it cannot be done goes through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: The ordering and exits are consistent with FR-007 (make static once, crate-scoped checks while iterating). Nothing requested is narrowed.

decisions.summary: runlock's wait reads time through a Clock seam (now, sleep) on the Taker: Wall (Instant, thread::sleep) in a run, Stepped in the test; the run's behavior and L7R_RUST_LOCK_CEILING (wall-clock seconds) unchanged

A red gate on correct work costs a make static rerun, which is the time the request's improvement 2 and FR-013's perf priority are about; nothing the GM asked for is narrowed and the run's behavior is unchanged.

decisions.summary: the test asserts exactly 6 waiting lines (0 to 50 ms, refused at 60) on the stepped clock where it asked >= 2
decisions.why: A tighter assertion on a deterministic event count, shown red with the behavior broken (left 1, right 6). Not the struck bitwise-exactness standard: it holds no port to a replaced output, it checks the wait's own behavior.

decisions.summary: a wait that never ends reads the stepped clock past READS=100 and panics rather than hangs
decisions.why: Makes the never-ends failure a red test instead of a hang; shown red with the ceiling broken. Enforcement of the fix, no new behavior in a run.

decisions.summary: the crate's other runlock tests keep the wall clock (two_runs_in_one_target_directory_take_turns at a 60 s ceiling against two 0.1 s calls; a_refusal_is_the_checks_reply asserting a refusal only), so Wall stays covered
decisions.why: Neither has failed; both stayed green 5 of 5 on the shared core that failed the old test 10 of 10, one has about 300x headroom and the other asserts nothing timed. A difference from T35's 'never a bare wall-clock bound' wording with no wrong outcome is not a defect (constitution XIV), so leaving them is not a defect left and needs no ruling; they also keep the Wall path covered.

decisions.summary: the task is performance work under FR-013 by its [perf] tag, not filed with PERF=1 (no engine stage's operations or time)
decisions.why: FR-013 names both routes ('filed with PERF=1 or tagged [perf]') and counts a task making the gate or the builders' loop faster; the choice of route is inside the requirement.

decisions.summary: the land-tooling half of the finding is folded into T20; T35 is independent of the other lanes
decisions.why: Ordering and task boundaries only; the land-tooling wall-clock finding stays owned (T20), nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: Split tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh into three shards (41 + 9 + 5 of its 55 checks), each making its own state
decisions.why: The split FR-010 / D17 / improvement 5 asks for, applied to one of the three named suites; every case still runs; shards 1.3/7.5/5.7 s alone, under the about-20 s bar; measured to save about 6 s of an incremental run and to cost nothing measurable in a full one.

decisions.summary: test-sync-with-main.sh is left whole (its split was built, measured and reverted); its full-run 26.8-40.2 s past the 20 s bar is now stated in found-and-left
decisions.why: Improvement 5's stated purpose (request.md) is that these suites 'set the floor on every make hooks-test', and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put the point as speed ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'). The block's measurements show the split defeats that purpose: full runs equal HEAD (mean 44.0 vs 43.9 s), the incremental run after a sync-with-main edit is slower with it split (12.7/12.1 s all-three vs 11.8/11.8 s l7r-gate alone), and its shards (8.7 + 7.7 + 4.0 s) cost more than the 5.0-7.7 s whole. It does not set the wall: re-read from the named logs /tmp/t21m/r1-4 and rm1-4-head-j8-c22.log, entry-gate finishes 10.1-14.8 s after it in every one of those eight runs, and its range 26.8-40.2 s matches them (40.2 is rm1, a run whose entry-gate took 51.5 s and which the entry-gate list drops as overlapped; without it 26.8-31.0 s - the stated range is the wider, not a hidden one). The earlier gap (SC-004's letter missed by a second suite, undisclosed) is closed: it is disclosed with figures and reasoning. Leaving a GUESS bar (D17) unmet with no wrong outcome is not a defect left (constitution XIV), so this is not deferral of a defect.

decisions.summary: test-entry-gate.sh is left whole, past the about-20 s bar in a full run (38.6-44.4 s); its case-4 chain of record gates is filed as its own performance task (T40, per the dispatch)
decisions.why: Same purpose test against request.md improvement 5. Splitting by its two cases does not lower the floor: full runs equal, and after an edit of it the split is slower (23.1/23.3 s vs 22.4/22.8 s whole); the wall is its case-4 chain, which a case split cannot shorten, and more job slots did not help. The literal split would ship a measured slowdown under the name of a speedup. The ruling rests on the chain being pursued as its own task so the request's purpose (entry-gate no longer setting the floor) is not dropped; the dispatch states it is filed as T40, an open [perf] box, which under FR-013 / SC-006 goes first. The 20 s bar is a GUESS, never a gate (D17); the request names no figure.

decisions.summary: Shard helpers copied into each shard rather than sourced from a lib file, so l7r-guard deps keys them
decisions.why: Implementation means of the split, following T20's shard form; changes no scope.

decisions.summary: Three pointers to test-l7r-gate.sh repointed to test-l7r-gate.3.sh; the seven to test-sync-with-main.sh left as the suite stays
decisions.why: Consequence of the kept split; the enumeration states its search (git grep of the three names).

decisions.summary: Fix test-parts.1.sh (unsets PARTS_MAX) and test-pair-hooks.sh (one part runs as its own process), both red in every PARTS_MAX=1 run
decisions.why: Suites failing on good work are defects found while doing this task (a wrong outcome, constitution XIV); fixing them as found is the standing rule, and they blocked measuring the job counts this task needed.

decisions.summary: HOOKS_JOBS stays 8 after measuring 6, 8, 12 and 16
decisions.why: No change made; the measurement shows higher counts add CPU-seconds and no wall.

decisions.summary: entry-gate's case-4 chain filed as its own performance task
decisions.why: Serves improvement 5's purpose (a faster hooks-test) and the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements' (FR-013); adds no departure from requested scope.

decisions.summary: Close T39 with no code change: a FRESH=1 run that waits on the target-directory lock runs its own tests (runner log: 10 of 10 executions over 5 concurrent FRESH runs; T32's two runs each wrote their own build and test Phase rows); the claim that a waiter replays the holder's result is withdrawn.
decisions.why: The task asked whether a FRESH run could report green without running. The measurement and the code reading show it cannot, so there is no wrong outcome to fix. Withdrawing a claim the measurement refutes is what constitution XIV asks for. Nothing in request.md or FR-013 is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Leave as it is that the rust-checks summary line quotes only the first `test result:` line of a crate's cargo test.
decisions.why: This is a display difference, not a wrong outcome: per the section, a failure in any binary fails the crate and prints cargo's full output. The GM did not ask for it, and it is not a defect under constitution XIV. The section says why it is not a defect, which is what FR-009 requires.

decisions.summary: Leave the matching 4.21 s figures unexplained, labeled as a GUESS (chance under load).
decisions.why: Both runs executed, as the Phase rows measured on 2026-11-20 show, so the match is not a sign of replay and there is no wrong outcome. Leaving a harmless coincidence unexplained narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: T39 stays a [perf] task under FR-013 and closes with no change.
decisions.why: The section records the task's existing FR-013 classification. It adds no scope and removes none.

decisions.summary: The one cited-text writer (`paragraphs` in bundle.rs, shared by build, foreign and requirements) runs each match to the next match or next heading instead of the first blank line, so a cited decision or requirement reaches the reviewer whole with its lists and tables.
decisions.why: Serves FR-013 and the approved improvement 4 ('Fewer plan re-rounds'): the cut text cost T17's and T19's reviews a round each. It widens what the reviewer is given; it narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A match written as a list item (bulleted requirement or decision) stops at a blank line its own indented lines do not follow (`item_end`), and no longer carries a following heading; a requirement written as a heading is read as before.
decisions.why: Same purpose as the writer fix: the reviewer gets the item's own text, nested lists included, and not an unrelated heading. The 43 decisions and 3 requirements that shrink lose only a heading line the old cut wrongly carried - a defect fixed in the task, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: No size cap is added to spec-cited.md; the bundle grows (T18's +6.7%, all decisions +5.6%).
decisions.why: Carrying the cited text whole is the point of the task; adding no cap keeps nothing out. Feature 375 amendment 11's lean bundle (cited text, not the plan) is kept, since only cited items are carried.

decisions.summary: T37 is filed as a [perf] task under FR-013.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the builders' loop faster, and the request's approved improvement 4 names fewer plan re-rounds as a time saving; a decision cut at its colon costs a review round. This is FR-013's own definition applied, not a carve-out from it.

decisions.summary: The heading-carry defect found while doing the work is fixed here, pinned by a red-first test.
decisions.why: Fixed in the task, nothing deferred; consistent with fixing known defects as found.

decisions.summary: Add `make format FILE=<path...>` and `make format CRATE=<dir>`, which format only what they name; bare `make format` is unchanged.
decisions.why: A [perf] task on the builders' loop under FR-013, which comes from the GM's 2026-11-20 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'. It is also the same kind of fix as approved improvement 2 (a crate-scoped step while iterating instead of a whole-tree one). Nothing asked for is narrowed, since the whole-tree form stays as it was.

decisions.summary: The one-file path feeds the file to the toolchain's rustfmt on standard input, run from the file's directory (so rustfmt.toml is found), with --edition taken from the owning crate's Cargo.toml (2015 where it names none), and writes the file only where rustfmt passed and changed it.
decisions.why: This is how the requested behavior gets done. Standard input was chosen on a dated scratch measurement showing that a path argument rewrites the file's `mod` children, which would break 'formats only what it names'. The plan's step 9 records that `--check --crate` was clean after FILE= runs, so the output matches cargo fmt.

decisions.summary: A Cargo.toml edition that is not a literal (for example an inherited one) is refused on the FILE= path.
decisions.why: This refuses an input it cannot read rather than guessing an edition and formatting wrongly. CRATE= and bare `make format` still cover such a crate. It does not narrow anything the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: FILE=/CRATE= format takes no run lock and never waits on another run's tests, because it builds nothing.
decisions.why: This serves the performance purpose (FR-013, the builders' loop) and does not narrow any requirement.

decisions.summary: FILE= given together with CRATE= is refused (exit 2), and the `format` failure's tip names CRATE= and FILE= instead of bare `make format`.
decisions.why: Usage guarding, and pointing builders at the scoped forms, serve the task's own purpose (not rewriting another builder's in-progress files). Nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Found and left (a): the make-only guard does not refuse a bare `rustfmt`. Deferred to T33 (held writes through a route the guard does not read), which lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is a narrowing because the block calls it a defect (a check that lets bad work through), and approved improvement 4 makes fixing in the task the default for briefs. FR-009, judged against its index line only since the bundle carries nothing more, requires a deferral to state why the defect is not fixed here, and this one does. The guard is rust/guard, where T31's builder has work in progress. Fixing it inside T34 means editing, linting and covering a crate that holds another builder's half-done files, which is the clobbering of in-progress work that T34 exists to stop, and T34's green exit cannot be met honestly over that crate now. So a literal fix-in-task would defeat the task's purpose. The defect is not left: it is filed in this feature as T33, with an order (before T22), and T33's class (writes by a route the guard does not read) matches it exactly.

decisions.summary: Found and left (b): the make-only guard's block message advertises bare `make format`, which rewrites every crate. Deferred with (a), 'Filed as T33'.
decisions.why: Ruled separately from (a), because a message's wording is not a 'route the guard does not read' and T33's class argument does not reach it. Only the location argument carries it. That argument is enough: the message text lives in rust/guard, where T31's builder works now, so the same purpose-level and exit-level reasons as (a) apply. The interim harm is reduced inside T34 itself, since `make format`'s own failure tip and `make help` now name FILE= and CRATE=. The block's 'Filed as T33' covers its whole bullet, both the guard gap and the message, so T33 owes the message fix as well as the refusal. A T33 that fixes only the refusal would leave (b) unfixed.

decisions.summary: Feature 204's D5 ('every python3 -c is a write') narrowed: a -c program a denylist of known writers judges read-only (read-mode opens only, no substitution/expansion, no relative or locally-answerable import) is marked how=read and is no write, unless the command also runs Python from stdin.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of feature 451's request or spec (the D5/D6 in spec-cited.md are 451's own decisions; 204's D5 is known only as the plan quotes it). Ruled anyway. rulings.md is empty, so the session's own ruling carries no weight; the ground is the constitution's defect definition: a guard that refuses or rewrites a read refuses good work. D5's premise ('its cost is now zero') is measured false where no clone resolves (80 corpus rows refused clone-unresolved, 79 rewritten, replay 2026-11-20). D5's purpose (no false allow) is kept by the conservative conditions and the stdin rule (parse#72, window#61 refused as before). The denylist ends in '...', so its full reach is not visible in the bundle; not a finding.

decisions.summary: A -c read stays a write when any segment of the same command runs Python from stdin (python3 -, heredoc, < file, | python3).
decisions.why: Keeps T31 from turning measured heredoc writers (parse#72, window#61) from refused into allowed; it adds no allowance.

decisions.summary: Three real heredoc reads (main-tree#147, window#339, window#361) stay refused or rewritten, as before T31, as the stdin rule's cost; recorded under Found and left and homed in T42, which retires the stdin rule once stdin bodies are judged, landing before T22.
decisions.why: The previous round's BLOCKED asked for exactly this: the known defect now has a home. Found and left names the three rows, how they were found (the replays' rows that moved back against the stage-1 build, each hand-read), why T31 does not fix them (no stdin reader exists, and lifting the rule without one lets parse#72's and window#61's writes through - trading a refused read for an allowed write), and a filed task (T42) that retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged, ordered before T22. T31 does not worsen these rows (they were refused or rewritten before it). Limit: T42's own task line (said in the dispatch to commit to retiring the rule, red first on these three rows) is not in the bundle; the block's own words 'which retires the rule once stdin bodies are judged' are what was read.

decisions.summary: Four rows that also run a script (main-tree#103 scratch script; window#60, #62, #308 the mirror's own test suites and hooks), refused or moved before only by the -c write, now run as typed without being shown to write nothing.
decisions.why: T31 changes nothing about how a script run is judged: the same commands without the -c read are allowed today, so their earlier refusal was a side effect of the defect fixed (a read misjudged as a write). The hand-read found no writer in any of the four, unlike parse#72/window#61, so no defect is shown, and keeping a misjudged read refused to cover an unjudged segment would keep the defect. Item 1's 'every write is still moved or refused as before' slightly overstates this for these rows; item 4 discloses it.

decisions.summary: Judging Python heredoc/stdin bodies for writes (301 corpus rows main-tree allows before and after) deferred to T42, landing before T22.

The restated goal still serves the request: the incremental run, the common case, fell 2.2-5.9 s per alternated pair with the suite still setting its wall, and the suite alone fell about 3.7 s. Dropping the full-run target cuts nothing the GM asked for. The measured reason it cannot be the target (once cut, the suite no longer sets the wall, and the cuts remove no CPU work) is a physical limit on what this task's files can reach, not a convenience.

decisions.summary: Measure the failure in a scratch clone first, then change only the launcher's build-failure path; no gate crate changed.
decisions.why: A [perf] task under FR-013 (the builders' loop). The GM asked that performance work go first (2026-11-20) and named no mechanism for this one; confining the change to the launcher narrows nothing he or the spec asked for.

decisions.summary: On a failed build the launcher keeps cargo's report and adds each file cargo points at (from the tree root), an advice line (yours: fix it; not yours: leave it and re-run once it compiles) and the git status of uncommitted edits; a failure naming no file keeps the old line; it applies to any uncompiling source.
decisions.why: Serves FR-013's 'the builders' loop faster': it removes the old order to edit the neighbor's file. It does not change who is refused or when, so it adds no behavior beyond the message. Its red-first shard case (2 FAIL lines on the unfixed launcher) only checks that the message is there, so it enforces the task and is not added scope.

decisions.summary: Do not build a fallback that runs the last good l7r-gate binary when the tree does not compile; the launcher stays fail-closed.
decisions.why: Neither the request nor the spec asks for a fallback. The GM's words call only for performance work to go first, and FR-013 defines it by tag. Not building one keeps existing behavior the plan must keep (feature 449 T061's fail-closed launcher, and the dispatch's rule that a gate check over a changed guard uses the new code), so it narrows nothing asked. If you read it against the task's own problem statement (others' commands blocked), it is still not a narrowing of the GM's request. On the merits it would be LEGITIMATE anyway: a fallback would let verdicts and push-trusted records come from a binary older than the code it judges, which defeats what the gate is for. The plan measured how much a fallback would cover: the commands that may run safely on an old binary were 787 of 12,700 make targets in a week (6%), and make decide (449 runs) and rust-test (2,414 runs) would still fail.

decisions.summary: Rule: a command may run on a binary older than the tree only if it renders no verdict and writes no record a later gate or push trusts. Under it decide, task-start, every check, rust lint/test/cover/dead, format --check, speckit-todo's push routes, mode-a and hamlet fail; format writing, bare speckit-todo and coord lines pass.
decisions.why: It is the reason for not building the fallback, not an exception put into behavior: nothing in the plan runs an old binary under it. It is narrower than (and so consistent with) the fail-closed launcher. The plan's figures carry one-shot measured labels (2026-11-20, .git/tool-usage.jsonl kind:target, 2026-11-13 to 20), and the arithmetic holds (787/12,700 = 6.2%).

The recorded figure is 1,531 lines cut and marked, 0 cut unmarked. In this bundle's spec-index.md, each line without a mark ends at a full stop, and the two cut lines (FR-006 at the cap, SC-001 after its sentence) end ' [...]'. Under the arbiter's ruling, where a marked cut falls, the cap and the sentence heuristic's boundary are not defects. Aside, not a finding: spec-index.md's heading names only the 420 cut as marked.

The plan's own own_run wording treats 'in N's' as naming another source, so it cannot also read those ids as bare. This is the T42 failure the task exists to end: the wrong feature's text, unmarked. It is a known defect left, and Found-and-left does not list it. It is not of the kind the arbiter excluded, which concerned where a marked index cut falls. Fix: read ids in a clause naming feature N as N's (looked up there, or NOT FOUND), with N's own name read as this feature's; or at the least carry them marked, as the bare form is. How often this occurs in real plans is not measured in this bundle.

decisions.summary: the racing a_quiet_session_is_ended_and_a_working_one_left_alone is replaced by a counted-check test of every path (no branch turning on elapsed time) and one threaded test of a stall ended and a watch halted

decisions.id: T47-D3 the work tests' timing left as it is
decisions.summary: the queue tests in runner/work/tests.rs, whose empty-proc pass count varies with scheduling, are left unchanged; line 281's cover is held by the counted check
decisions.why: Structurally, per the plan's reading of work.rs and the stub, no halt can beat a check and the 30 s sleep is the one wall-clock margin, so no assertion turns on the varying empty-proc count; the green runs (30/30 idle, 10/10 pinned, 1.6-5.2 s each) agree. A difference that works, not a defect, so leaving it needs no ruling (constitution XIV v2.36.0).

decisions.summary: T47 is classed as performance work under FR-013 by the [perf] tag, since a gate red on correct work costs a builder a rerun of make static; not PERF=1 because it moves no engine stage's counted operations or time
decisions.why: FR-013 names the tag as one of its two forms and counts a task that makes the gate or the builders' loop faster. A cover that refuses correct work is a defect (a check refusing good work, constitution XIV) whose cost is a rerun of make static, the unit the request's improvement 2 was measured in. One observed miss and none reproduced in 60 fresh covers makes the saving small, but the class is the task's kind, not its size.

decisions.id: T47-D5 449 FR-008 met on the measured minimum
decisions.summary: the threaded test's 0.06-0.32 s under a host load of 44-52 is read against the no-thread test's 0.06-0.19 s in the same batch, so the spread is the host's and the test's own cost is under a tenth of a second
decisions.why: Not an exception to FR-008: the plan claims compliance, and its 0.06 s minimum over 35 runs is under the bound, beside a control test with no thread at the same floor. It argues the rule is met, not set aside.

decisions.summary: make static once at the end after crate-scoped checks; independent of the other lanes, T45 sharing only the target directory under the run lock; red is recorded and set down, a claim of impossibility ruled by make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Follows FR-007's crate-scoped loop with one make static, and the project's standing exits; nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The flip is attributed to the replay's mktemp directory name (run.py8Q), not timing; the timing hypothesis is set aside on a forced-name reproduction (exactly T42's 8+3 rows) and a 30-run load series at 0.
decisions.why: Deciding the cause from measurement is how the task is carried out; it narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: NAMED_PATH becomes [\w./-]+\.(?:md|py|sh|toml|json)\w*(?![\w/]): a file, never a directory on the way to one; extensions keep trailing letters (.jsonl, .pyc) so those writes keep their old verdicts; the \b variant rejected after it changed four probe payloads.
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (the guard went silent on a write it should correct, by the letters of a random directory name) found by this feature's own step, which constitution XIV's fix-as-we-go asks to be fixed before the next step; keeping .jsonl/.pyc as before changes nothing else the guard does.

decisions.summary: GM_REQUEST's open-ended pattern is left as is; HELD_SHAPES and PROSE_FILE already end bounded.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome is shown: a longer name it catches is only reported, never silenced or corrected wrongly, so leaving it is a difference, not a defect left (XIV's definition).

decisions.summary: The hook wrapper's 45 s build limit (L7R_GUARD_BUILD_SECS, feature 449 T004/D7) is left as the one bound on time, deliberate and outside the replay.
decisions.why: It did not cause the flip (the replay ran its binary directly, and the forced-name replay reproduces the flip without it); no wrong outcome is shown, so leaving it is not a defect left.

decisions.summary: Red-first test, fix-deleted re-red, forced-name replay at 0, crate checks, 100% guard-crate coverage, make static once, one landing.
decisions.why: Verification that the fix does what it is for; it adds no behavior and honors FR-007's one-static-run purpose.

decisions.summary: The section states T45 is not performance work despite its [perf] tag, leaves the tag's removal to the coordinator, and says its start is owed FR-013's escape with the reason 'a defect found by this step'.
decisions.why: It may put a non-performance fix ahead of open performance work (if one was open at T45's start; the bundle does not show it), which narrows the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'. Legitimate because the exception is implied by the GM's own standing rule, not request.md but constitution XIV's fix-as-we-go (the GM 2026-11-18: 'we should fix all known bugs in each step before moving on'): the defect is a guard silent on a write it should correct, found by this feature's own step T42. The section does not carve the case out of FR-013: it reclassifies the mis-tag honestly and says FR-013's own escape is owed (owed, not yet recorded). One landing does not defeat the order's purpose ('doing those first makes everything after them faster').

decisions.summary: D6 is built in the event-log writer, event_log_hooks.rs (guard-edit first), reusing T26's filed.rs for the task
decisions.why: Where the FR-004 writer lives is implementation; D6 already puts the cost and task on the event log's Agent and SubagentStop lines.

decisions.summary: filed::filed takes an Agent call's task from its prompt's FIRST line where the description names none; the feature stays the description's; never a later line
decisions.why: D6 states it word for word: task from its description, else its prompt's first line. Leaving the feature on the description only keeps free prompt text from setting more than D6 asks for; it does not narrow FR-004's task.

decisions.summary: fields::agent_cost writes tok {in, cached, created, out} and ctx on every SubagentStop
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for input, cached input and output; D6, the accepted spec, already settles created and ctx. Nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: The transcript is the payload's agent_transcript_path, else the transcript beside the session's, read whole row by row
decisions.why: D6 names agent_transcript_path. The fallback widens where a cost can be found, it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Reuse context_cap_hooks' row reader (call_of split out of usage_of; context and own_transcript made crate-visible, no copy)
decisions.why: Implementation choice. It changes no behavior anything asked for.

decisions.summary: The last row of each message.id stands for its call, so each call is counted once
decisions.why: D6 says each message.id is counted once. Item 4's measurement (dated, method named) shows a sum over rows would overcount output by about 2.7x, so the rule does what it says it is for. The replay in item 9 matches R2's sum to the token.

decisions.summary: A stop with no transcript, or no call in its transcript, writes neither tok nor ctx
decisions.why: FR-004 puts a cost on every stop line, so this is a case the rule does not cover. But without a transcript the cost cannot be known at all, which is a real physical impossibility. Writing zero would put a false figure on the log and defeat SC-002's purpose of reproducing the retrospective's numbers. It is one case, and it stands alone.

decisions.summary: A user row with usage, a non-JSON row and a synthetic zero row are not calls (no tokens, no context)
decisions.why: This defines what counts as a model call under D6's count and ctx's 'last call'. Such rows are not model calls, so leaving them out excludes no real cost.

decisions.summary: A builder with no meta file is still costed and carries no task
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for a task only where the dispatch names one, and D6 takes the stop's task from the meta file. The cost is kept. Only a task that cannot be known is left off.

decisions.summary: The hook never refuses
decisions.why: FR-004 is logging. It asks for no refusal (FR-012 covers only FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013).

decisions.summary: After T04, before T10; one landing
decisions.why: Sequencing. FR-004 sets no order, and the GM's 2026-11-20 priority on the six improvements concerns the order of those tasks, which this block does not reorder.

decisions.summary: The transcript read adds 0.27-0.35 s to each agent stop (against 0.04 s), once per stop, accepted; the block declares itself not performance work
decisions.why: The cost is measured and dated, and it is paid once per agent stop, not per tool call. The request accepted a stop-time record ('records it at each agent's stop'). No defect is left: nothing reads wrong and no tool hangs.

decisions.summary: Done when the fixture cases are green and the T202 stop replayed through the built guard writes R2's figures to the token
decisions.why: Verification of FR-004 itself. It enforces the request and adds no scope.

decisions.summary: Part 1: guard_write reads an inline interpreter body (Python literals resolved where the shell stands, -c/heredoc bodies as commands, Perl/Ruby/Node by the same literal reading, a for loop's variable per word), with a literal only read, a subprocess argv and a dict value exempt.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T14 hole (a heredoc rewrite of a guard source). The three exemptions each answer a measured false refusal of correct work (replay round 1: window#56, #299, #312, #267), and no real write in the 1,134 rows passes through them. That is a precision choice inside the task, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: A shell or interpreter write of a guard file stays refused under a live guard-edit permit, as sed -i is at HEAD; the permit is for the Edit tool.
decisions.why: This keeps HEAD's rule for sed -i and extends it to the new forms. It narrows nothing, because the compliant route (the Edit tool under the permit) remains, and the block message names it.

decisions.summary: A bare rustfmt is refused as bare-rustfmt, and the message names make format FILE= / CRATE=.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T34 hole, with the compliant command named.

decisions.summary: shell_write refuses a write that the walk or a Python literal places in the gated tree while its gate runs. Only a literal that resolves to a path where the shell stands counts, and an unresolvable path fails open, as the walk does.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T34 hole (git apply / cp under a running land). Failing open on an unresolvable path is the gate's existing rule, not a new carve-out, and the 18 outside-the-tree rows it lets through were measured as correct work.

decisions.summary: A literal handed to a function of the program's own is counted where the shell stands (fail-closed). window#72, a correct write into another clone that HEAD allowed, is now refused under a running gate. Left unfixed, filed as T49, lands before T22.
decisions.why: This is the only item T33 leaves that makes HEAD worse. By the block's own account window#72 is a correct write that moves allowed->refused, a check refusing good work, which is a defect by constitution XIV. It contradicts the section's goal 1 ('nothing correct is refused by the new reading') and its constraint 2 (XIII, no known regressions). The reason given, that placing the literal needs the function's body and no reader of interp does, is a cost argument. It meets none of the criteria: nothing is physically impossible, the request implies no such case, and fixing it would not defeat the request's purpose. The block also stretches one justification over two unlike guards. It cites make-only's fail-closed count for this literal, while it states gate-write's own rule as failing open on a path it cannot place. The available escape (GATE_WRITE_OK, or waiting for the gate) does not make a false refusal correct, and a feature whose purpose is efficiency is worse off for a guard that stops correct work. FR-009's form (why, id, order) is met, but the form is not legitimacy. To clear it, window#72 is not refused by what lands in T33, or the section gives a reason that meets one of the three criteria.

decisions.summary: chmod's mode and chown's owner are no longer read as files (shared/tree.rs tool_paths).
decisions.why: Fixes HEAD's own false refusals that the replay found (refusals#132, window#256), as FIX AS WE GO requires.

decisions.summary: git_output reads the writing options of the read-only subcommands (--output, archive -o, format-patch, bundle create, bugreport, diagnose). stash list/show are reads, and the gate's commit-or-add rule reads git's subcommand, not the word anywhere in the segment.
decisions.why: Closes the observed T44 hole (git diff --output read as a read). The stash and commit-or-add changes fix false refusals the replay measured (parse#148, #171, #173, #229, refusals#88, window#279), plus one the new check would otherwise have introduced.

decisions.summary: The addition reading twelve git subcommands outside GIT_WRITES as writes was built, measured and dropped, and filed as a measure-first task T50, lands before T22.
decisions.why: The observed hole (git diff --output) is fixed. What is left is inherited from HEAD, and no wrong outcome is recorded for it: the replay of 1,134 rows caught no real write with the addition, and its only moves were its own false refusals. Under the defect definition nothing defective is left, so the drop does not narrow the request. The dispatch's and the session's rulings are not the GM's and carry no weight here; this is judged on the end state alone.

decisions.summary: A program run from a file (python3 script.py) is not read. One real case was found (window#215 rewriting a clone's Makefile), plus seven clone writes the gate would see. Filed as T51, lands before T22.
decisions.why: I read this as a fifth form outside T33's four observed holes, not as part of hole 1. Hole 1's mechanism reads a body handed inline to the interpreter, and a script file is a separate artifact needing a reader no guard has. HEAD has the same gap (T33 does not worsen it). It was found by a census the section records with its method, and it is filed with an id and an order under FR-009. If hole 1 were read as covering every interpreter write, this would be a narrowing whose reason (cost, plus the need for its own replay) meets no criterion. I chose the narrower reading of the task's observed forms.

decisions.summary: DEPTH 3 for nested bodies, stated as a convention past any shape in the corpora.
decisions.why: Measured as covering every row; it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: After T14 and T15, lands with T07, one landing. Exits include make static once, plus rust-test, lint, format, cover, quick and hooks-test.
decisions.why: Sequencing and exits consistent with FR-007 (make static once) and the guard rules.

decisions.summary: Performance work? no.
decisions.why: A classification. Whether T33 may start while a performance task is open is FR-013's guard's call on task state that the bundle does not carry; it is not a decision of this section.

decisions.summary: Each archived deferral is read by hand once and gets one verdict (carried / fixed / still open, filed / not a defect); ticked tasks' history is not re-judged
decisions.why: This applies D15 (a deferral needs a filed task and an order) and constitution XIV (only a wrong outcome is a defect) to the deferrals T17's replay found. It does not narrow either one: every deferral gets a named carrier, a commit, a filed task or a stated reason it has no wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: make work-budget reading only the roll's stages is ruled not a defect, because make work-budget-review (T224) re-counts every Mode A sheet stage (placer, compound, pipeline) and holds it to twice its budget
decisions.why: The deferral describes how the work is split between tools, not a wrong outcome. The row says, with the files and the dev/work-budget.json keys read at HEAD as its measurement, that every Mode A stage is counted and held by another target. A stage would have to go unchecked for a check to be passing bad work, and none does. Under XIV v2.36.0 leaving this as it is stays within what was asked and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: a pool-sheet stage has no change, raise or accept path; filed as 449 T243
decisions.why: Filed as an open task with its evidence (the header of sheets.rs read at HEAD). The work is not left undone.

decisions.summary: the reviewer's notes (an unstated radius, a 'ten zones' slip, the fire gap) are ruled not a defect
decisions.why: No total moved by more than a few operations, T152 held both sheets within twice their budget, and the slip is in the prose of a SOUND derivation. No map, check or research finding is wrong, so under XIV this is a difference, not a defect.

decisions.summary: the Python cache's old entries under .gencache/<map>/ are ruled not a defect (disk only)
decisions.why: Nothing reads them: the Rust cache's DIR is .gencache/rust. Disk used in one clone is not a wrong map, a wrong check or a crashing tool.

decisions.summary: 449 T156, T200, T218, T219, T221a, T224, T239(1)(3) are carried by named tasks, each ticked at a cited commit or open (T240); T239(2) was fixed by T238
decisions.why: Each deferral names the task or commit that covers it. Nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: the shared make-call reading class is censused (13 modules through shared::make; 10 own readers, up from 8 now that measure_hooks' has() and gate_write_hooks' head_of are found) and filed as 451 T52, measure first, landing before T22
decisions.why: The census states its search space as D15 and the enumeration rule require: greps of rust/, scripts/ and the Makefile, rechecked with git grep at HEAD and a grep for "make literals, each hit read. The fix is filed with an order rather than left. Measuring first follows XIV: whether any of the 10 gives a real command a wrong verdict has not been shown yet.

decisions.summary: process-table argv readers, cheap contains("make") prefilters, batching_hooks' NOT_RECON, log-field readers and research prose are set apart from the T02 class
decisions.why: The class is reading which make targets a command text runs. Process-table readers read a live process's argv, where a wrapper is its own process. Prefilters only skip work. batching_hooks only tests whether make is present, can never refuse wrongly, and was read at cited lines. Log-field readers read an already-parsed field. Each is set apart for a stated, checked reason. That is defining the class, not carving a case out of it.

decisions.summary: T03's deferrals: three fixed at commits; the lines filed by feature.json carried by T26, with the remainder in T53; booking by make carried by T08 (open); the live line fixed (66 make static lines carry cat tests); the two unmatched data-model rows ruled not a defect
decisions.why: Every item has a carrier, a commit or a filed task. A row that never matches books nothing wrong, so it has no wrong outcome under XIV.

decisions.summary: POLL_CHECK_S going into D14's knob table is carried by T22 (open)
decisions.why: D14's knob table is T22's line. It is carried, not dropped.

decisions.summary: (a) events-refile still owed and (d) the indexes missing filed.rs and refile.rs, both filed as T53 (narrowed to the one builder checked); (b) two re-file judgment calls on closed features and (c) another builder's uncommitted work stopping make static ruled not a defect; (e) fixed by T07
decisions.why: The open items are filed with a measured remainder (19 lines, from make events-refile DRY=1). (b) is history between the reports of closed features, with the copy from before the re-file kept. (c) is not a defect of the tree. Neither (b) nor (c) is a wrong outcome of the tooling.

decisions.summary: Found and left: none, since the three still-open deferrals are filed (449 T243, 451 T52, T53) and the two 451 filings land before T22
decisions.why: Filing the deferrals is this task's own work, and each one carries a task id and an order, so nothing found is left unfiled.

decisions.summary: Compile (the union of build and cover-build phases) is split out of ANY run a phase ties to, not only a tests run (data-model's wording); the critical path splits a main-session call's gap the same way.
decisions.why: D4's own text books compile 'inside the Bash call or background span that holds them', not inside a tests run; the GM asked 'how much time are we spending on recompiling things', and a landing's or gate's compile is recompiling. Widening the split books more of what was asked; it removes nothing.

decisions.summary: A phase ties to the run of its session whose span holds it and whose target is its make OR whose task is its task, ranked target, then task, then latest start; unmatched phases counted in the footnote, never dropped; a phase starting after the window is none of it.
decisions.why: D4 ties by session, clone and target; adding task as a second key moved 567 untied compile phases (60.9 min) to 170 (12.1 min), measured, so it brings more of the GM's compile time under its task (the per-task breakdown he asked for). It narrows nothing. Note for the caller: the block's restatement omits D4's clone key; since builders share the main session's id (D4), dropping clone could tie a phase to a same-task or same-target run in another clone. Not ruled on - the block is silent, not explicit - but confirm the code still keys on clone.

decisions.summary: A background run ends at the main transcript's queue-operation enqueue row naming its tool-use-id, before its BgEnd line's t.
decisions.why: D3 itself says a BgEnd's t is when the notice reached the session, not when the run ended (the notice waits while the session is mid-turn); the enqueue row is the nearer reading of the run's own end. More accurate booking of what was asked; nothing dropped - BgEnd remains the fallback.

decisions.summary: A background run with no enqueue row or BgEnd ends at the TaskStop call that stopped it (read from the session's and its subagents' transcripts), else open to the window's end.
decisions.why: A stopped run has ended; booking it open to the window's end was a wrong outcome (ten runs, 6,070 of 6,792 machine minutes booked 'other', measured). D3's 'open to the window's end' is the fallback for a launch with no end anywhere, and a TaskStop is an end. Adds an end source; narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: A subagent's call inside the main session's turn is booked on the critical path as what the session was doing (the call it waits on, or the model); between turns it keeps the wait open. The session's own line moves state before a zero gap is skipped, and SubagentStart/SubagentStop keep it.
decisions.why: D7 defines the critical path as the wall clock partitioned by what the MAIN SESSION was doing or waiting on; a builder's line cutting the session's make static in two misbooked the session's own state. This implements D7 literally; builder runs are still booked in the runs table (machine minutes).

decisions.summary: A call running several targets is booked by the first of them in PRECEDENCE (land, gate, tests, review, docs, spec-kit step, other) in both tables; a phase ties to a run that runs its make at all; a landing's gate and cohort phases are split out as gate, less the compile inside them.
decisions.why: FR-001/D2 book a call by its target and are silent on a line with several; the day's 19 landings were launched 'make claims-owed ...; make ledger-owed; make land' and booked review by their first target, which misses the land and gate columns FR-005 asks for (land 4.2, gate 0.0 against 27.4 min of their own gate phases, measured). The block's own cross-check (land 5.3 + gate 14.4 + compile 13.0 = 32.7 min against the end phases' 32.4) shows precedence absorbs almost no non-land time. Cohort booked as gate follows D5 (cohort-landing is the landing's gate stage).

decisions.summary: where-time shows a critical-path (wall clock) table and a runs table of every session's and agent's Bash calls in overlapping machine minutes, never summed into the wall clock.
decisions.why: D7 asks for the critical path 'and beside it the summed agent-minutes'; FR-005 'the wall clock on the critical path apart from the summed agent-minutes'. The runs table is that.

decisions.summary: UNTIL= passes --until (held Makefile edited); logs read to their end so a run still going at UNTIL is clipped there, not dropped.
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask for UNTIL=; clipping rather than dropping keeps the run's in-window time booked.

decisions.summary: 159 compile and landing-gate phases (9.5 min) tie to no run; left, counted and shown in the runs table's footnote, ruled 'not a defect'.
decisions.why: The time is shown, not lost: the GM's 'how much time recompiling' is answered with the footnote. No reader is told a wrong number; per WHAT A DEFECT IS, a gap counted and displayed is not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: feature-report is held unchanged here; its reading of the columns is T11's.
decisions.why: A task split inside the feature, not a removal: FR-005/D7 still require feature-report to read the same columns through the same functions, and the block assigns it to T11 rather than dropping it. Not verifiable from the bundle that T11's line carries it; the caller should confirm.

decisions.summary: A subagent's background run whose notice reached only its own transcript (the queued_command attachment) ends here at BgEnd, TaskStop or the window's end; reading queued_command is deferred to T09, lands before T10.
decisions.why: D3 says 'The readers (T08) ... read the subagent transcript's queued_command attachment', so this narrows T08 against D3's own wording. It is legitimate as a task-ordering narrowing only: the requirement stays in the feature (FR-002/D3), the block gives the why (D3's end-of-run work is T09's), the filed task and the order ('lands before T10') as FR-009 requires, and T09 is the very next task on the same reader. The GM's request sets no task order that this breaks, and the defect is not carried past the reader work. Not verifiable from the bundle that T09's section names it; the caller should confirm before ticking T09.

decisions.summary: The critical path still books 866 of 1,354 min 'waiting on work'; booking a wait to the runs in flight (D3, the FR-005/D7 'background run' column) is deferred to T09 and the critical path apart from the agents to T10; filed as T09, lands before T10.
decisions.why: This is the spec's headline wrong (SC-001: under a tenth unexplained; today 64%), so it is a narrowing of T08 and not a 'within'. It is legitimate on the same footing as the queued_command deferral: FR-002 and D3 assign wait-to-run booking a mechanism of its own (inflight on the Stop, else the holding launch), the block names the owner (T09, then T10 for D7's agent split) and the order, and the requirement and its success criterion are untouched. It also covers the 'background run' column FR-005 lists, which neither table carries yet. The deferral is legitimate only if T09 lands before any non-reader work; a spec where SC-001 is not met at the close would be a defect, not this.

decisions.summary: The critical path's model column (342 min) holds about 235.4 min between turns, because a turn's Stop line often lands in 449's log and the 451 walk never sees the turn end; reading a session's turn lines from every feature's log is folded into T10 (D5, D6), lands before T11. Two smaller wrongs the same check found (a builder's stop inside make static; the zero-gap skip) are fixed here.
decisions.why: A known wrong outcome left standing (model minutes booked that are really the session waiting), so a narrowing. Legitimate because the fix needs a decision that belongs to the critical-path design T10 owns (how a turn spent on another feature is booked against this feature's wall clock - D7's critical path apart from the agents), the block states why, the task and the order (before T11) as FR-009 requires, the smaller wrongs reachable inside T08 were fixed here, and the requirement stays in the feature. Not verifiable from the bundle that T10's task line carries it (the caller says it does). Ordering seam for the caller: T09's wait booking keys on the Stop that opened a wait, and those are the very Stop lines this item says land in 449's log; T09 should read them across logs or know T10 will, else T09's numbers are built on the same missing lines.

decisions.summary: A launch paired with its BgEnd, else the subagent transcript's queued_command row holding its tool-use-id, else open to the window's end; a wait booked to the runs its Stop names inflight, else to the launch whose span holds it (a Stop written before the field: the session's own runs/agents whose span holds the gap).
decisions.why: D3's reader half as written.

decisions.summary: Stop and UserPromptSubmit lines of the window's sessions read from every feature's log, kept once; a foreign Stop/prompt taken as 451's only when a line of the session's own lies between it and its paired line, else marked events::FOREIGN.
decisions.why: FR-002/D3 book a between-turns wait from the Stop that opened it; a misfiled Stop is otherwise invisible. Taking a foreign turn only when it holds 451's own lines keeps 449's turns out of 451's model. How the requested booking happens, not added scope.

decisions.summary: A left-out foreign turn books from its prompt to the session's next line of 451's own to a new column 'another feature' (247 min in T08's window), the waits between 449's turns among it, moving no state of 451's walk.
decisions.why: D7 partitions the critical path by what the main session was DOING or waiting on; while it worked 449's turns it was doing another feature, so that time is not 451's model, idle or waits, and showing it as its own column keeps it visible rather than hiding it - 'where our time went on that task' answered without crediting 451 with 449's work. This is the cure of last round's NOT LEGITIMATE item, applied window-wide: the column also takes minutes that had sat in model, in 'none', and with a 451 agent in flight (the agent share fell 945 -> 864, none 147 -> 3); that is consistent, since the session in those minutes was on 449's turns, not waiting on 451's agent. A column beyond FR-005's list is within, as T08's plan review/other subagent/idle columns are: D7's partition needs a bucket for it.

decisions.summary: SubagentStart/SubagentStop lines read from every log as the turn lines are; an agent counts for the feature only where a line of its own log names it.
decisions.why: D3 books a wait to the agents inflight names and an agent's span needs its start and stop lines (9 of 115 had their start only in 449's log, measured); the own-log filter keeps 449's agents off 451's waits. Inside D3.

decisions.why: FR-013 counts where-time's readers as performance work for ordering. The slower command is a measured cost, not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: The between-turn model minutes T10's line names are fixed here (model 342 -> 89); T10 keeps agent-minutes, tokens and rework, reading turn ends through events::turn_lines. The 253-vs-235.4 gap reconciled: 15.1 of the 18 min inside 449's own turns now booked another feature, 2.9 stated unreconciled, method given.
