Text to correct (not a narrowing): this bullet still says the 253 moved 'to the waits', but by the section's own tables waits rose only ~866 -> ~994 and the rest went to 'another feature'; and the Measured footnote's 992 min of waits disagrees with its own parts (120+864+9+3 = 996) and with the wait columns (994, 996 with review) by more than rounding.

decisions.summary: Idle 126 -> 0: the two stretches over an hour (08:32-09:35Z, 10:42-11:46Z) the session spent on 449's turns now book 'another feature' (123 min) and model (4 min), measured per stretch, with a red test (a_stop_in_another_features_log_opens_the_wait, red2/red3).
decisions.why: Last round's NOT LEGITIMATE item fixed in T09 as the cure prescribed: the session's time on another feature's turns is booked apart rather than to 451's runs or none, red first. Nothing is left, so no ruling is owed.

decisions.summary: A first SubagentStart with no meta file is filed by the Agent call that dispatched it (per-session side file <events dir>-dispatches/<sid>.jsonl), else by the session's unreturned calls of its type within WINDOW_S (300 s, GUESS), only where every candidate's brief agrees; a disagreement stays feature.json's, marked.
decisions.why: Booking each agent's time to the feature and task it served is the per-task breakdown the GM asked for (2026-11-19) and measurement work FR-013 counts as performance work; an agreed-only rule leaves the undecidable case marked rather than wrong. FIFO dropped on measured inversions is design, not scope.

decisions.summary: A command's F= with no T= of its own no longer overrides the brief's task; the brief wins unless the command carries its own T=, matching the re-file's BY BRIEF rule; a decision against T26's stated order.
decisions.why: T26's order was a plan decision, not the GM's words; reversing it so a builder's time is booked to the task its brief served implements the request's per-task breakdown more faithfully. Nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: filed.rs and fields.rs read F= and T= from strip_heredocs of the command, never from text quoted inside a heredoc; a quoted F="451" stays the command's own.
decisions.why: Fixes a measured wrong filing (lines booked to 385 from quoted test code); serves the per-task breakdown.

decisions.summary: A task-only brief is not matched to a task start more than 72 h (GUESS) before the line; such a line falls to feature.json's feature, marked fallback.
decisions.why: Fixes the measured 23-line misfiling into 385's log; a marked fallback is kept apart by readers, so the outcome moves from wrong to unattributed. Knob labeled GUESS with its distribution measured.

decisions.summary: rust/gate/crates/measure (T09's) is not edited; the writer converges on the re-file's rule instead.
decisions.why: Coordination between two tasks of the same feature; no part of the request is narrowed by it.

decisions.id: T53-6 the 23 written lines deferred to T56
decisions.summary: The 23 lines already written into 385's log are not moved here; filed as T56 (the re-file sharing the writer's stale-start rule), lands before T22, because the re-file lives in the crate T09 is editing.

Sequencing a fix within the same feature to a filed task is not a narrowing of what the GM asked. Note: T56 must actually move them, since they are misbooked time.

decisions.id: T53-7 older past-72h briefs in closed features
decisions.summary: 444's T42 (313 h) and 417's T46 (618 h) task-only lines left as they are; not shown to be wrong; the re-file does not reach those closed features.

decisions.id: T53-8 nested task-only brief now fallback
decisions.summary: A nested subagent whose brief names only a task and whose clone holds no fresh start of it is filed under feature.json's feature marked fallback, rather than by a stale start.
decisions.why: Moves such lines from booked-wrong to marked-and-kept-apart; nothing is booked wrong, and the common case (a fresh start, p90 1.8 h) still resolves to its task. An unattributed gap is not a wrong outcome under the defect rule.

decisions.id: T53-9 done measures and landing owe
decisions.summary: Red-first tests per shape, 702 passing; the dry run still moves 21 until the landing's live binary updates; one real events-refile owed at landing at the coordinator's timing, then a dry run showing 0 to move but the 23.
decisions.why: Verification of the requested data's correctness; enforcement of what was asked.

decisions.summary: One appended side-file line per Agent call half (about 150 bytes) and at most one 64 KiB tail read (TAIL, GUESS) at a meta-less first start; the hook never refuses or prints.
decisions.why: Design cost, not fidelity; keeps T26's constraints.

decisions.summary: Each agent's tokens are read from its agent-<aid>.jsonl usage rows inside the window, each message.id once, and the last SubagentStop tok is used only where no transcript row counts (a declared departure from D6's 'the reader keeps the last per aid').
decisions.why: Following the letter would defeat the request's purpose, which is an agent's token cost. By the block's own dated figures the stop's tok is short of the transcript rows on 16 of the 17 stops that carry one, and only 17 of 279 stops carry one, so reading it would report wrong costs. The stop line is still read as the fallback, so the request's 'read those new lines' and its cheap-history purpose survive for agents whose transcripts are gone. The writer defect is filed as T59 with why, id and order. Not settled from the bundle: whether the 262 stops with no tok at all are the same writer defect (T59 should cover an absent tok as well as a short one).

decisions.summary: Each agent is kept once with its kind and its task (first start's task from the launch brief per D6, else its first stop's) and booked by start to the task its lines name, or by tick to the mark at its first start. The old walk, which read only the 451 log and booked by the mark, is deleted.
decisions.why: D7 says 'each agent's span and tokens under its task', and D6 says where an agent's task comes from. It is read from every feature's log through T09's single build of the spans, as the dispatch states.

decisions.summary: Agent spans are cut to SINCE/UNTIL, overlapping spans are merged (a double start with no stop between counts once), an agent with nothing left is dropped, and token rows are limited to the window. The clip applies to the flight's agents only, so the time table is untouched.
decisions.why: D7 reports the window's wall clock with the agent-minutes beside it, so the agent-minutes are the window's. The dispatch names the clip and the single count of a double start, and the time table is measured unchanged line for line.

decisions.summary: A refused landing is a landing end line whose landed is false, never read from its exit code. A landing of several tasks is one refusal, counted under each task.
decisions.why: This is D7's and D5's definition word for word: 'landed is false', and 'exit 3 with its ticks standing is a landing whatever its code'.

decisions.summary: A plan re-round is any spec-fidelity or spec-fidelity-verify agent of a task after its first, each agent counted once (a resume is not a new round), with an agent naming no task counted as no task's re-round. The count therefore includes every spec-fidelity review dispatched under the task, not just its plan's rounds: 68 in the window, about 3x the feature report's 23 rounds past the first.
decisions.why: This is D7's parenthetical word for word: 'a task's spec-fidelity and spec-fidelity-verify dispatches after its first'. The request asks for no re-round count of its own, so the block narrows no clause. The block measures and discloses the 3x against the feature report's rounds-per-subject table, which is a different quantity. Whether D7's label 'plan re-rounds' overstates its own definition is a question about the spec, not this block.

decisions.summary: After the time table, where-time prints a by-task table (agents, agent minutes, k tokens in, k tokens out, refused landings, plan re-rounds, kinds) with an all row, a row per agent under its task, and a line setting the agents' summed minutes beside the critical path's wall clock. feature-report is wired by T11.
decisions.why: FR-005 and D7 ask for the critical path's wall clock apart from the summed agent-minutes, each agent's span and tokens under its task, and the rework counts. This is that output.

decisions.summary: The critical path, the turn ends and the between-turn model minutes are T09's and are restated, not rebuilt. The 2.5 min left unreconciled is not traced further.
decisions.why: The dispatch says T09's work is restated. The time table is measured unchanged, and an untraced 2.5 min (under 1%) is a difference, not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: The SubagentStop writer's short tok is not fixed in T10. It is filed as T59, to land before T22, because the writer is the guard's file, outside T10.
decisions.why: T10 is FR-005's reader. The writer defect is FR-004's and is fixed in this feature by T59, which carries FR-009's why, id and order. The reader routes around it meanwhile, so no wrong number reaches the report.

decisions.summary: The -0 minutes printed for a task row with no agent is fixed by folding the sums from 0.0, with a red-first pin.
decisions.why: A defect found and fixed in the task.

decisions.summary: The 12 agents (94 min) that name no task stay under no task.
decisions.why: FR-004 gives an agent a task 'where its dispatch names one', so an agent whose dispatch names none has none to be booked under.

decisions.why: The performance task the GM asked to be filed on 2026-11-21 ('yes please file that as a performance task'), [perf] under FR-013.

decisions.summary: the last 25 lines of each red check's log are printed (a GUESS)
decisions.why: An output detail of the requested target, labeled a GUESS.

decisions.summary: static_runs_hooks counts a make closing-checks as one make static run; STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK stays 2
decisions.why: Stops the new target being used to get round FR-007/D11's count. It enforces what was already asked and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: the event log books make closing-checks to tests (BUCKETS)
decisions.why: FR-001's one shared table, extended to the new target.

decisions.summary: the root CLAUDE.md's verification list states the order in one line
decisions.why: Documentation of the order. The refusal is the enforcement and this line carries none.

decisions.summary: the order at make decide (a decide after the caller's last code edit with no closing-checks started after it) is a NOTICE, not a refusal
decisions.why: Unchanged since the last round, which ruled it LEGITIMATE. A refusal at decide time cannot tell the closing tail from a decide in mid-build, because that depends on code edits that have not happened yet. The replay has 30 of 75 firings wrong (40%). Refusing anyway would force a closing-checks run on unfinished code, and that run counts toward FR-007's STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK=2, which defeats the performance purpose.

decisions.summary: a foreground make static, make hooks-test or make closing-checks (chained, piped, under timeout, the main session's) is REFUSED, red first, naming run_in_background and make closing-checks, recorded blocked; escaped by FOREGROUND_OK="<reason>" (recorded escaped, a bare token refused); STATIC_OK does not stand it aside; judged on every command of a chain before the decide notice; both refusals heard at once
decisions.why: This is the fix the last round asked for. The rule is now real enforcement in D12's form, carries FR-012's red-first test (708 passed, 3 failed on a stub; the suite's case 9 at 26 passed, 8 failed; then green at 711 and 34/34), and has a recorded escape for the cases where it is wrong. For static and hooks-test, the separate replay the last round asked for was done and stated in words: 55 foreground calls (27+28), 5 on correct work (4+1), 50 right (34 after the last edit + 16 mid-build; 19+9+6 and 11+5). That is 9%, set against the decide rule's 40%, and no FR-007 collision, because a backgrounded run is the same one static run. The arithmetic checks. A refusal implements the requested order. It is not a narrowing of it. Refusing make closing-checks rests on the earlier ruling, which is acceptable because the log has no foreground call of it to replay.

decisions.summary: a foreground make quick, the third closing check, is not refused (implicit: the refusal names static, hooks-test and closing-checks only)
decisions.why: The block does not label this, but it is a decision. The finding's cost is the slow checks run in the foreground one after another, and quick takes 1 to 5 s (item 9's timings). By item 4's own counts, the 51 foreground closing-check calls after the last edit (35.0 min) less the replay's 34 static/hooks-test calls (31.2 min) leave about 17 calls and about 4 min for quick. Inside closing-checks, quick already runs beside the others. Not refusing it does not gut the purpose. The decide notice still tells the order, and the slow checks are enforced by refusal.

decisions.summary: the refusal of a foreground make closing-checks is not replayed (no PreToolUse line names it) and rests on the plan review's ruling
decisions.why: Nothing could be measured because the target did not exist in the log. The refusal is the stricter side of the request, and T22 reads its blocked and escaped rows.

decisions.summary: a code edit made by a Bash write (sed -i, heredoc) is not seen by the decide notice: it can miss, never wrongly fire
decisions.why: A stated limit of a notice that has already been ruled legitimate. It refuses nothing, and the foreground refusal does not depend on it.

decisions.summary: the closing tail's idle minutes on later tasks' transcripts, the notice's noticed rows, and the refusal's blocked and escaped rows are read on T22's measured day; the mechanism's own before/after (104 s in sequence vs 52 s at once) is measured now
decisions.why: The effect in the world can only be read from transcripts of tasks that do not exist yet. The mechanism's own before/after is measured in the block, and T22 is the close's measured day that FR-013 names. The line now covers the refusal's blocked and escaped rows as well. The same caveat applies as last round: T22's own text is not in this bundle, so the session has to confirm that T22 takes these rows.

decisions.summary: item 4's recount: 93 calls by 38 builders after their last code edit, 51 foreground (35.0 min), 39 background, 3 refused by other guards; 28 builders decided after their last edit, 21 before any check; the earlier 92/56/33 reading explained
decisions.why: A restated measurement, not a decision about scope. 51+39+3=93. The difference from the first reading is put down to the pre-T04 bg rule and to the log having grown.

decisions.summary: make static is left unchanged because its Phase lines show it builds and runs no plain test; the double build is moved to where it actually happens, make rust-test after a green coverage pass, by widening T111's keep
decisions.why: The task line asked for static's plain build and test to be dropped. Measured Phase lines (dated, per target) show static has neither, so dropping one is impossible. The plan goes after the duplication the line was about (a crate's tests built in rust-test and again in coverage), which serves the GM's perf-first ordering (request.md 2026-11-20/21).

decisions.summary: a binary is refused only where it holds a test, cfg(test) or mod x; a doc fence is refused only where it is not a text block; eleven crates join the keep
decisions.why: This is the mechanism by which the covered run answers for the plain run wherever it actually does, which is what the task line asked. The plan measures each new admission (binaries read, fences listed, no integration tests, examples or benches).

decisions.summary: checks is excluded for its cfg(not(coverage)) test
decisions.why: The covered run genuinely does not run that test, so it does not answer for checks' plain run. The line's own scope is 'where the covered run answers'.

decisions.summary: rustc is excluded because its tests contain cfg(coverage) as text, which the conservative predicate refuses
decisions.why: A forgone saving, not a wrong outcome. T111's premise (no code reading cfg(coverage)) is applied as written, and nothing passes untested. This is a difference from the most a change could save, not a defect under XIV, and it narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: make rust-test is unchanged but for has_doctests, which now shares unit_tests_only's reading (holds_doctest), so the five text-only crates skip a cargo test --doc pass that ran no test
decisions.why: The constraint 'rust-test's fast uninstrumented loop unchanged' exists to keep the loop fast and uninstrumented, and it still is: no test stops running (all 10 fences are text, measured), and only an empty pass goes. A single reading keeps the keep and the run in agreement. This speeds the builders' loop, which FR-013 and the GM's perf priority cover.

decisions.summary: land's --all-features plain runs of pool, rust/mode_a and rust/phases are left
decisions.why: The coverage run (default features) does not answer for an --all-features cfg, so this falls outside 'where the covered run answers'.

decisions.id: D7a feature unification, T111's existing keep
decisions.summary: crates T111 already kept (owed, claims, land, trials) have covered tests run under unified features
decisions.why: Not T57's decision. It is T111's standing keep, reported as found and left, and no wrong outcome is shown.

decisions.id: D7b feature unification, rust/gate newly kept
decisions.summary: T57 adds rust/gate to the keep, though its covered tests may run with owed's testkit (which switches owed's entry_lines seam) while its own plain build lacks it
decisions.why: Here the covered run answers under unified features, not the crate's own. The bundle shows a difference but no wrong outcome: the gate (make done, the push) already rests on the coverage run alone for these crates, and the crate's lint runs on its own features. Under XIV, a difference with no wrong outcome is not a defect, so leaving it needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: no verdict key carries the environment; attributed to T93, not new with T57
decisions.why: The plain run's own key already has the same exposure, so the keep adds none. The tests T32 found were fixed. No new defect is left.

decisions.summary: the guard's refusal of the builder's Edit and Write in a kind:bg dispatcher's clone is filed as T62 rather than fixed here
decisions.why: A defect (a tool refusing valid work) that T57 leaves. The deferral meets FR-009: it says why it is not fixed here (the fix is in rust/guard's clone_sync_hooks, where T58 works in this clone, and a guard edit rebuilds the gate crates T58 is counting), names its filed id (T62) and gives its order (lands before T22, the close). So it is fixed within the feature, before the close.

decisions.summary: after T55, beside T58, before T22; green and red exits; one landing
decisions.why: Scheduling inside the feature, consistent with FR-013, and it touches nothing T58 owns.

decisions.summary: T57 is a [perf] task under FR-013
decisions.why: The GM, 2026-11-21: 'yes please file that as a performance task'. It makes the builders' loop faster.

decisions.id: T62-D1 parked_by as the backstop's third dispatcher source
decisions.summary: clone_sync_hooks::parked_by treats the session whose record's parkedJobId equals this session's own jobId as its dispatcher, after L7R_DISPATCHER and forked_from, read in one pass over ~/.claude/sessions/*.json
decisions.why: Fixes a measured defect (a check refusing good work: the parked job's first edit of a clean clone refused, its builder falling back to exact-replacement scripts that skip every Edit and Write hook). That fallback defeats the GM's 'make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement and not just instructions' (2026-11-19), and fixing known defects as found is the standing rule. It follows the same dispatcher pattern forked_from and L7R_DISPATCHER already carry, and widens nothing past the job's own parker.

decisions.summary: an empty jobId, parkedJobId or session id matches no record
decisions.why: Keeps the new source from matching every record that lacks the field; it keeps the backstop as strict as before for anything that is not a real parked job.

decisions.why: Keeps the backstop's purpose (docs/session-clones.md) whole. The refusal is lifted only for the claimant's own parked job, and the red-first shell twin ('did NOT park -> still blocked') pins that.

decisions.id: T62-D4 no rule for a parker that starts a new conversation
decisions.summary: the unmeasured case of a parked interactive session keeping parkedJobId under a new session id gets no rule
decisions.why: No such record was found, so a rule would be a guess. Leaving it out narrows nothing the request or spec asked for; the task's line names only parkedJobId equal to this jobId.

decisions.id: T62-D5 the claim restated by measurement, tasks.md line left as filed
decisions.summary: 'refuses every Edit and Write' restated as 'the first edit of a clean clone, the job's main thread included'; T62's tasks.md line kept for the dispatcher
decisions.why: A claim the measurement contradicts is fixed by restating the claim (constitution XIV). The fix covers the measured scope, which is wider than the builder-only reading, so nothing is narrowed.

decisions.id: T62-D6 edit scope and isolation from T57/T58
decisions.summary: edits only in clone_sync_hooks and its tests, the shell suite, two docs rows and this section; T57's rustc crate and T58's worktree untouched
decisions.why: Limits the change to the defect's own mechanism and adds nothing unrequested.

decisions.summary: after T57's Found and left filed it, before T22; 'Performance work? no'; budget one landing
decisions.why: A guard fix that measures and speeds up nothing is correctly classed as not performance or measurement work under FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words, so the scheduler sees it as it is. Whether starting it ahead of an open performance task needs an escape is FR-013's guard's call at start time, and this section does not override it.

decisions.summary: red-first Rust test and shell case, the crate's tests, lint, format, coverage, dead code, and the replay that allows the job and refuses a stranger
decisions.why: Tests that fail only when the requested fix is absent, plus a pin that the stranger is still refused. This is enforcement of the fix, not unrequested scope.
